item.title: Nineteen jailed over deadly Moscow concert attack
item.summary: Gunmen opened fire at Crocus City Concert hall near Moscow in 2024, killing 149 and injuring more than 500.

item.title: Iran's new supreme leader vows to block Strait of Hormuz in first statement
item.summary: A message attributed to Mojtaba Khamenei also says Iran will continue targeting US bases in the region.

item.title: Death toll from Ethiopia floods and landslides rises to more than 100
item.summary: Forecasters say storms are becoming more intense in the region, partly due to global warming.

item.title: Senegal approves tougher anti-gay law as rights groups raise concerns
item.summary: "Violence and fear" will spike and "equality and non-discrimination" will be trampled on, warn critics.

item.title: No evidence Swiss bus fire was terrorism, officials say
item.summary: Initial reports suggest a man with "psychological problems" set himself on fire on the bus, according to police.

item.title: France's ghost car scandal that allowed one million illegal vehicles onto the roads
item.summary: Fake dealerships were manipulating the state vehicle licensing agency's official records, France's auditor has found.

item.title: China approves 'ethnic unity' law requiring minorities to learn Mandarin
item.summary: The law states that children should be taught Mandarin before kindergarten, until the end of high school.

item.title: Parents accused of hiding daughter's HIV infection and neglect
item.summary: The child did not see a doctor until she was six - and had not had any vaccinations, Italian media say.

item.title: The Pussycat Dolls confirm reunion: 'We're celebrating where we're at as women'
item.summary: Nicole Scherzinger, Ashley Roberts and Kimberly Wyatt announce a new single and world tour.

item.title: Kanye West ordered to pay $140K in Malibu mansion renovation lawsuit
item.summary: A handyman had sought $1.7m (£1.267m) from the rapper over claims of unpaid work, medical expenses and being unfairly fired.
